doc.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999

title: Replacing his brother Teddy in Gene Krupa's band
summary: Marty sat in at the 400 Club, was offered Krupa's job when his brother had left, and went to California for films.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Teddy, yeah. That’s a funny story too, because I was working at Childs’ Paramount with Henry Jerome’s band. And there was a — oh a little ginger ale does it — and there was a club on Fifth Avenue and 43rd Street, called The 400 Club. And I was working with Henry up there, at 42nd Street and Broadway, and after the job I went to see Krupa’s band because I knew they were working at this club. And when I walked in, the band, I don’t know whether they had just taken a break or they had played the last number, something, but Joe Dale was the manager of the band. He was a drummer whenever Gene stood in front of the band he would play the drums, Joe Dale. So he came to me he says, “hey Marty, would you like to sit in with the band?” You know these things happen to you like you’re taken aback. I said, “yeah, I’d love to.” So I played a set with the band see? And when I got off Joe came to me and he says, “you know Gene likes you very much, would you like to join?” I said, “what are you kidding? My brother’s with the band. I would never do that.” He says, “no, he gave his notice” he was leaving the band. I said, “well I’ve got to find him.” And you know I couldn’t find my brother anywhere. I didn’t know what happened to him. Maybe he got annoyed because I was sitting in, and he figured somebody’s going to take his place, maybe some guy from left field would come in. Here’s his own kid brother sitting up there. I don’t really know. We never discussed it or anything. So anyway I took the job with the band, and I went with the band. And why did I say that story? Oh because—
Yeah, we were talking about Krupa, this was 1945.

’46, ’46. Yeah. So anyway I went with the band and what happened was I know it broke my brother’s heart because he was with the band for some time, and I go with the band and we went to California, we did two movies, a movie and a short. Now I know that broke his heart. What could I do? I didn’t tell him to make a movie so I could be in it. So
